nodes.name: Keep Valid Documents

options.systemMessage: You answer document questions using only the retrieved knowledge-base context. If the context does not contain the answer, say so and set needsHuman=true.

nodes.name: Answer from Knowledge Base
nodes.notes: The AI brain: reads the input, decides which attached tools to call (and in what order), then composes the answer. Watch out: Every iteration is a billed LLM call. Max Iterations is the cost ceiling. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run.

nodes.name: OpenRouter Chat Model
nodes.notes: Chat model powering the AI step (model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5). Swap providers here without rewiring. Credential: OpenRouter API key. openrouter.ai/keys → create a key.

parameters.toolDescription: Semantic search over the classification knowledge base. Always call this before answering factual document questions.

nodes.name: Knowledge Base Retriever
nodes.notes: Exposes the vector index to the agent as a semantic-search tool. Credential: Pinecone API key. app.pinecone.io → API Keys, and create the index first.

nodes.name: Query Embeddings
nodes.notes: Embedding model — MUST be the same model for indexing and querying, or retrieval quality collapses. Credential: OpenAI API key. Same OpenAI API key as the chat model.

nodes.name: Rerank Retrieved Chunks
nodes.notes: Re-scores retrieved chunks so only the most relevant reach the model. Credential: Cohere API key. Same Cohere API key.

nodes.name: Grounded Answer Found?
nodes.notes: Two-way gate on ={{ !($json.output || '').includes('needsHuman') }}. TRUE continues the happy path, FALSE takes the alternate branch. Watch out: The false branch carries the non-matching items — wire it deliberately rather than leaving it dangling.

nodes.name: Return Answer (HTTP 200)
nodes.notes: Sends the HTTP 200 response back to the caller — keep this fast; heavy work happens after/async. Watch out: Only works when the Webhook node's Response Mode is set to 'Using Respond to Webhook node'.

nodes.name: Log Knowledge Gap
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Document Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Flag Gap to KB Owners
nodes.notes: Sends an email via Gmail — subject is the first line of the message body, recipient comes from the item's email field. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Google OAuth2. Google Cloud Console → enable Gmail API → OAuth consent screen → OAuth client ID (Web).

nodes.name: Fingerprint for Idempotency
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Build a stable idempotency key per document (djb2 hash, no deps) Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Drop Already-Processed Items
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

nodes.name: Serialize Run Output (CSV)
nodes.notes: Serializes items to a CSV binary file.

# Run an assistant workflow: Google Sheets & Gmail, webhook

**Pattern:** AI Agent · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Webhook

## Overview

Fires when a webhook arrives, and covers classification work end to end across Google Sheets, Gmail and Slack.

It moves through 20 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. Receive Inbound Webhook
2. Keep Valid Documents
3. Answer from Knowledge Base
4. OpenRouter Chat Model
5. Knowledge Base Retriever
6. Query Embeddings
7. Rerank Retrieved Chunks
8. Grounded Answer Found?
9. Return Answer (HTTP 200)
10. Log Knowledge Gap
11. Flag Gap to KB Owners
12. Fingerprint for Idempotency
13. Drop Already-Processed Items
14. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
15. Archive Row Snapshot
16. Load Previous Snapshot
17. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
18. Summarize Run Stats
19. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
20. Send Summary to Gmail

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing classification work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Receive Inbound Webhook → Keep Valid Documents → Answer from Knowledge Base → OpenRouter Chat Model → Knowledge Base Retriever → Query Embeddings → Rerank Retrieved Chunks → Grounded Answer Found? → Return Answer (HTTP 200) → Log Knowledge Gap → Flag Gap to KB Owners → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Row Snapshot → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Gmail → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Google Sheets and Gmail aligned by hand for classification
- Answering classification questions from your own indexed documents, then replying in Google Sheets
- Classification work that needs a judgement call per item before it reaches Google Sheets
- Pushing classification events into Google Sheets and Gmail the moment they land, not on the next poll

## You get

- Keeps Google Sheets and Gmail in step for classification, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Google Sheets or Gmail are skipped, across all 23 nodes of this classification build
- A failed Google Sheets or Gmail call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 23 nodes in this classification build
- The classification AI step is isolated from Google Sheets, so models swap without touching the other 23 nodes
- Fans the same result out to Slack in the same run, for classification

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Cohere API key; Google OAuth2; Google OAuth2 / service account; OpenAI API key; OpenRouter API key; Pinecone API key.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Retrieval happens *inside* the agent as a callable tool, not as a mandatory step before it, so the agent decides when a lookup is actually worth the latency instead of always paying for one. The 'Grounded Answer Found?' gate treats an honest 'needsHuman' as a valid outcome, not a failure — logging the gap so the knowledge base improves beats a confident hallucination.

## Practice exercises

Already production-grade — deepen your understanding:

1. Turn the reranker knob on and compare answer quality on a deliberately ambiguous question.
2. Swap the vector store provider — only the vector store node changes, nothing else in the workflow.
3. Lower topK from 5 to 2 and see how much retrieved context the agent actually needed.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**OpenRouter API key**
openrouter.ai/keys → create a key.
_Gotcha:_ One key reaches many models — handy for fallback.

**Pinecone API key**
app.pinecone.io → API Keys, and create the index first.
_Gotcha:_ The index's dimension must match your embedding model exactly.

**OpenAI API key**
Same OpenAI API key as the chat model.
_Gotcha:_ Indexing and querying MUST use the same embedding model or retrieval breaks.

**Cohere API key**
Same Cohere API key.
_Gotcha:_ Rerank is billed separately from embeddings.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Google OAuth2**
Google Cloud Console → enable Gmail API → OAuth consent screen → OAuth client ID (Web).
_Gotcha:_ Add n8n's OAuth redirect URL exactly as shown in the credential, or the consent loop fails.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Webhook returns 404**
Cause: Calling the test URL when the workflow is published, or vice versa.
Fix: Test URL works only while 'Listen for test event' is armed; the production URL needs the workflow published.

**AI node fails with an auth or quota error**
Cause: API key missing billing, or the per-minute rate limit was hit.
Fix: Confirm the provider account has credit. For rate limits, lower concurrency or switch to a higher-quota model.

**The AI returns the wrong shape or rambles**
Cause: The prompt is under-specified for the task.
Fix: Tighten the System Message: state the role, the constraints, and the exact output format you expect.

**Retrieval returns nothing or irrelevant chunks**
Cause: Index is empty, or indexing and querying used different embedding models.
Fix: Run the ingestion workflow first, and make sure both sides use the identical embedding model.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Gmail: request the narrowest send/read scope the nodes need — full mailbox access is rarely required.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole classification payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.

The webhook path is unguessable but it is not authentication: add header auth or an IP allow-list before this endpoint is reachable from the internet.

## 🤖 AI cluster

Purple nodes form one AI unit: the root node orchestrates, sub-nodes plug in via typed ports (model / memory / tools / parser). Swap the chat model without rewiring anything else. Costs scale with tokens — keep prompts lean and cap iterations.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your classification process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.
